facts.text: On August 28, 1963, Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his 'I Have a Dream' speech to 250,000 people in Washington D.C. — a crowd larger than the entire population of Orlando, Florida at the time.
On August 28, 1937, Toyota was incorporated — it began as a division of a loom company, and Japan now exports more vehicles annually than the entire EU combined.
Monaco is so densely populated that if Texas had the same density, it would contain more people than exist on Earth.
The Philippines is the only country in the world with no land border and no shared language with any of its neighbors.
More people live within a 25-mile radius of Manila than in the entire country of Australia.
On August 28, 1963, while MLK marched on Washington, the Dow closed at 750. It has since risen over 5,000% — compounding quietly behind every headline.
On August 28, 1996, ValueJet rebranded as AirTran after its Everglades crash. The rename worked: AirTran was eventually acquired by Southwest for $1.4 billion.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792 with 24 brokers and 5 securities. It now lists companies worth more than most continents.
Saudi Aramco briefly surpassed $2 trillion in market cap in 2022 — making a single state-owned oil company worth more than every listed company in Germany, France, or the UK.
The Swiss franc is so stable that a chart of its value against gold over 50 years looks nearly flat. Most national currencies on the same chart have vanished.

On this date in 1789, William Herschel discovered Saturn's moon Enceladus. We now know it vents liquid water into space — making it one of the strongest candidates for extraterrestrial life in our solar system.
Your skeleton is not the rigid scaffold it appears. Bone is a living tissue that completely replaces itself roughly every decade, quietly rebuilding you while you sleep.

On August 28, 1963, 250,000 people gathered on the National Mall. The human brain encodes crowd experiences differently than solitary ones — mass emotion physically synchronizes strangers' heartbeats.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh approximately one billion tons on Earth.

Oxygen is technically a byproduct of pollution. Cyanobacteria invented photosynthesis around 2.4 billion years ago and flooded an atmosphere that had never contained free oxygen, triggering a mass extinction.
On this day in 1963, Martin Luther King Jr. delivered 'I Have a Dream' — to a crowd smaller than a sold-out NFL game, yet it restructured the moral language of a civilization.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was ancient history to ancient Egyptians.
On this day in 1845, Scientific American published its first issue. It is older than the safety pin, the dishwasher, and the electric lightbulb.
The fax machine was invented in 1843 — 26 years before the transcontinental railroad was completed. You could fax someone before you could efficiently cross the country.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Europe's oldest university predates Tenochtitlan by three centuries.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Coined by John Koenig in 2012, it behaves like an ancient word because it fills an ancient need.
Sonder (n.): the realization that every passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Koenig invented it; the world adopted it as fact.
On this day in 1963, Martin Luther King Jr. delivered a speech whose title, 'I Have a Dream,' was improvised mid-sentence at Mahalia Jackson's urging.
Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word for the shared glance between two people who both want something but won't say so. Yaghan has fewer than five remaining native speakers.
On this day in 1830, the locomotive Tom Thumb raced a horse-drawn railcar outside Baltimore — and lost. Steam won the war anyway.

On this date in 2012, Satoshi-era wallet 1HQ3Go3ggs8pFnXuHVHRytPCq5fGG8Hbhx moved 80,000 BTC — the single largest dormant-wallet transfer ever recorded at the time, triggering immediate speculation about Satoshi himself.

On this date in 2017, the Bitcoin network hit a then-record 490,000 unconfirmed transactions in its mempool, a direct catalyst for the SegWit2x compromise that would fracture the development community weeks later.

Ethereum's uncle rate — orphaned blocks still rewarded to reduce centralization pressure — peaked near 9% in 2017. No other major proof-of-work chain has ever successfully sustained partial rewards for losing miners at scale.

The Bitcoin genesis block contains the embedded text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — but it also has a 50 BTC coinbase reward that is provably unspendable, because early Bitcoin code couldn't reference block 0 as a UTXO.

Uniswap v2 introduced the TWAP oracle by storing cumulative price sums rather than snapshots — an elegant fix to flash-loan manipulation that costs an attacker exactly one full block of capital to corrupt even briefly.
On this date in 2012, Alex Krizhevsky submitted AlexNet's ImageNet results — a 10.8-point error gap over second place that ended a decade of hand-engineered vision features overnight.
On this date in 2018, Google Brain published 'Speech2Face', reconstructing facial features from voice alone — accurate enough to infer age, gender, and ethnicity from audio.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 US households, spent in weeks.

Chinchilla scaling laws, published in 2022, revealed that most large language models at the time were undertrained relative to their size — the field had been building bigger models when it should have been feeding them more data.
The first neural network to defeat a professional Go player, AlphaGo, used a policy network trained on 30 million human moves — then discarded human data entirely in AlphaGo Zero, which was stronger.
